column_semantics: The schedule uses a single Interest Rate column for debt and a single Dividend Rate column for preferred equity. For PIK debt, the stated Interest Rate is the all-in current coupon and the PIK component is shown parenthetically within that stated rate; it is not a separate additive rate outside the printed Interest Rate. Preferred equity rows that are wholly PIK print the dividend rate as the PIK rate itself.

rationale: The filing presents one Interest Rate column rather than separate cash and PIK columns. On floating-rate PIK debt, the displayed total rate is paired with Reference Rate and Spread columns and the PIK amount is parenthetical inside the displayed Interest Rate, for example 9.97% (5.00% PIK), SOFR, 6.25%. That format means the 9.97% printed rate is the all-in coupon, with 5.00% of that total paid in kind. Preferred equity rows with only PIK dividends likewise print the Dividend Rate as 12.50% PIK or 14.50% PIK.
